chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding what came in the Hadith that the 'awrah (nakedness/vulnerability)' of the believer is prohibited upon the believer, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not that he uncovers him so you see something from him. Rather, it is that you report against him or fault him.'

key_terms.تَرْوِيَ: To report, to narrate (often implying reporting against someone)
key_terms.تَعِيب: To fault, to criticize, to find defect
key_terms.عَوْرَة: Nakedness, vulnerability, or that which is exposed

ai.seo_question: What does 'awrah of the believer' mean in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the concept of 'awrah from physical modesty to social and spiritual integrity, defining it as the protection of a believer’s reputation from backbiting and criticism. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'ghibah' (backbiting) as a violation of the believer's sacred honor, reinforcing the ethical duty to guard one another's dignity in community life. By linking physical exposure to verbal exposure, the hadith underscores that revealing a believer's faults is as serious as uncovering their body.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar, from Zayd,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding what came in the Hadeeth that the nakedness of the Momin is Prohibited upon the Momin, heasws said: ‘It is not that (by which) he uncovers him so he sees something. But rather, it is his reporting against him or faulting him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al- Husayn ibn Mukhtar from Zayd from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) the following: “

About the Hadith that says, ‘Privacy of a believer is unlawful for another believer,’ the Imam has said, ‘It is not that they (genitals) are exposed and one sees certain parts of them. It is to make certain narrations against him to reproach and defame him.’”
